assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 400,000 samples/s peak. 99% is the write path (remote-write from scrapers), 0.6% alert-rule evaluations, 0.4% (1,600/s) dashboard queries. Monitoring systems are overwhelmingly write-dominated and this ratio is the point.

assumptions.subject: dashboard_query
assumptions.statement: One dashboard load is modelled as 12 cache lookups (visit_prob 12.0) — one per panel — and 1.8 block reads on the misses. That fan-out, not the query count, is what sizes the query tier.

assumptions.subject: writer
assumptions.statement: The writer appends to an in-memory head block and flushes one compacted block per ~200 samples (store visit_prob 0.005). Retention, downsampling and compaction cost are not modelled.

assumptions.subject: query
assumptions.statement: A query instance sustains only ~600 rps because range queries are expensive; service time is set at 60 ms. Cardinality explosion — the failure mode that actually kills these systems — is NOT expressible in this engine: it changes the cost per query, and the engine takes cost per query as a fixed input.

assumptions.subject: cost
assumptions.statement: Compute only. Block storage GB-month and object-store request charges are excluded, and for a long-retention deployment they are the largest line.

_library.summary: Write-dominated metrics platform: remote-write ingest through a log into a TSDB writer, with a cached query tier for dashboards and alerting.
